author: zicokolter
text: @mmirman @hadisalmanX This is how I interpret what's being presented in these plots.  On the other hand, I think there are still structural reasons to be interested in exact verification methods, but validating a specific test set metric just isn't one of them. (3/3)

author: zicokolter
text: @mmirman @hadisalmanX All test set bounds are, in some sense, a high probability guarantee about performance on the "true" population.  Adding one more high probability doesn't seem like a bit deal at all if our goal is to assess actual (adversarial) generalization performance. (2/3)

author: zicokolter
text: @mmirman @hadisalmanX There may be a few too many endpoints to this thread that it's hard to disentangle it all, but I wanted to add a quick comment here.  I personally don't feel like the 99.9% probability makes it an unfair comparison to our deterministic bounds.  (1/3)

author: zicokolter
text: New work with @_powei, @priyald17, and Bryan Wilder on (SDP-based, differentiable, approximate) SAT solving as a layer within deep networks.  For example, learns to play 9x9 Sudoku just from examples, without any structure provided (past work like OptNet never scaled beyond 4x4).
